checked_claims.note: Z→U is a finite étale right S_6-torsor, so over Q averaging is exact and Gr^W_16 H_c^16(U;Q)=Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z;Q)^{S_6}=M_[6]. FND-0165 supplies the corner injection Gr^W_16 H_c^16(U)→Gr^W_16 H_c^16(A) for the open immersion of separated finite-type C-schemes (a connected component of a smooth atlas of the finite-type balanced Hurwitz stack is of this type; the parenthetical 'locally Noetherian' wording is not an extra generality). A→S is a Zariski-locally trivial P^2-bundle once h^0(L_s)=3 identically (packet FND-0139/FND-0142) and Grauert is applied on the reduced base, hence proper, so Rπ_!Q=Rπ_*Q=Q⊕Q(-1)[-2]⊕Q(-2)[-4] as constant Tate objects. Compact-support cohomology of A is therefore H_c^*(S)⊕H_c^{*-2}(S)(-1)⊕H_c^{*-4}(S)(-2) as MHS even if S is not proper, and Gr^W_16 of that sum is the displayed three-term target. The argument never identifies H_c(U) with H_c(A).

S_5 fixing one letter acts freely on the S_6-torsor, so Z^(1)=Z/S_5. Rational transfer gives Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z^(1))=Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z)^{S_5}. The S_6→S_5 branching rule removes one box: only [6] and [5,1] restrict with a trivial S_5 summand, each with multiplicity one, so the source is M_[6]⊕M_[5,1] as multiplicity Hodge structures (not the full isotypic subrepresentations). FND-0166, whose remaining hypotheses (CE)+(N)+(BAL), reduced locally Noetherian base, h^0=3, and fibrewise base-point-freeness of L (packet FND-0130/FND-0134) hold on the balanced chart, identifies Z^(1) with the reduced-support open in the universal divisor script-D and identifies script-D→script-C with a Zariski-locally trivial P^1-bundle. FND-0165 then injects the corner of Z^(1) into that of script-D, and the proper P^1-bundle formula identifies the latter with Gr^W_16 H_c^16(script-C)⊕Gr^W_14 H_c^14(script-C)(-1).

Under (H-S), the three summands in the first target are Q(-8), Q(-7)(-1)=Q(-8), and Q(-6)(-2)=Q(-8). Polarizable pure Q-Hodge structures of a single weight are semisimple, so a subobject of ⊕Q(-8) is again ⊕Q(-8); this is an honest Hodge-structure statement rather than a semisimplification. Duality Gr^W_16 H_c^16 dual to W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16} with no extra Tate twist (FND-0165's convention) sends Q(-8) to Q(8). Over Q, |S_6| is invertible and S_n-irreps are self-dual, so invariants equal coinvariants and T_16(U)=T_16(Z)^{S_6}.

Under (H-C) both summands of the second target are Q(-8). Semisimplicity makes the multiplicity spaces M_[6] and M_[5,1] sums of Q(-8). The rational representations V_[6] and V_[5,1] are pure of type (0,0), so the full isotypic Hodge structures V_λ⊗M_λ are likewise sums of Q(-8), and their Borel–Moore duals are sums of Q(8). No claim is made about other partitions.

Correctly recorded gap, not a defect in the stated conditional theorem: (H-S) and (H-C) are hypotheses, the remaining S_6-isotypics are uncontrolled, FND-0164 blocks replacing that missing work by a nonconstant-coefficient Leray weight-floor argument, and no Gysin, support-exhaustion, or comparison map to M_{6,6} is asserted. Confirming the lemma does not verify C66-TATE-SUPPORT or discharge RED-0001.

theorem_statement: Sharp rational Tate-transfer criterion for the balanced Z-model. Let S be a connected reduced locally Noetherian complex scheme in a smooth chart of the balanced genus-six degree-four Hurwitz stack, with no component image contained in the type-(ii) locus. Let p:𝒞→S be the pulled-back universal curve, L=W_5⊗ω_p^{-1}, A=P_S(p_*L), U⊂A the reduced-support locus, and Z=Ord(U) its finite étale right S_6-ordering torsor. Write Gr^W_16 H_c^16(Z;Q)=⊕_{λ⊢6} V_λ⊗M_λ. Then there are natural injections of pure weight-16 Hodge structures M_[6]→Gr^W_16 H_c^16(S;Q)⊕Gr^W_14 H_c^14(S;Q)(-1)⊕Gr^W_12 H_c^12(S;Q)(-2) and M_[6]⊕M_[5,1]→Gr^W_16 H_c^16(𝒞;Q)⊕Gr^W_14 H_c^14(𝒞;Q)(-1). Consequently, if Gr^W_{2j}H_c^{2j}(S;Q) is a sum of Q(-j) for j=6,7,8, then T_16(U)=T_16(Z)^{S_6} is a sum of Q(8); and if Gr^W_16 H_c^16(𝒞;Q) is a sum of Q(-8) and Gr^W_14 H_c^14(𝒞;Q) is a sum of Q(-7), then the [6]- and [5,1]-isotypic parts of T_16(Z):=W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(Z;Q) are sums of Q(8).
